instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.66 prohibits any person from lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed under §13.63, and §13.63(1)(a) provides for obtaining that license to act as a lobbyist.
A lobbyist license expires on December 31 of each even-numbered year, which establishes a biennial (24-month) renewal cadence.
Lobbyists must obtain a license (§13.63) while principals separately file a registration statement (§13.64) and file separate written authorizations for each principal-lobbyist relationship (§13.65).
The lobbyist license application must include items such as the applicant’s social security number (or sworn statement) and signature, but §13.63 does not require submitting a photograph.
Section 13.621(3) exempts elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees from specified lobbying provisions when acting in an official capacity.

Section 13.621(2) provides that an agency filing a statement under §13.695 and named officials are not subject to several lobbying requirements (including licensing/registration/reporting sections) except as provided in §13.695, creating a partial exemption for government agencies.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled provisions specify initial lobbyist licensing and principal registration requirements but do not state a deadline for amending a lobbyist’s license/registration information (e.g., address changes); amendment obligations/deadlines, if any, are not included in the provided text.

The statute requires licensure/authorization before engaging in lobbying as a lobbyist (§13.66), but it does not set a numerical 'days after first lobbying' registration deadline for lobbyists; the concept is effectively pre-activity, so no day-count can be extracted as an IntCell from the text.
